verdict.content_summary: Not a tool or article but a raw task directive: an imperative spec instructing an AI assistant or dev team to refactor a codebase until LOC drops at least 30%, delivered as either one monolithic pull request or a staged PR series. Its substance is prompt-as-spec — a hard, measurable objective (a deletion quota) paired with a structured deliverable format (PRs) that routes agent output into a normal review workflow. The value is as a reusable template for driving coding agents, not as software to adopt. It's thin on its own but mechanism-dense for anyone already running agents against their own repos.

grabs.what: Quantified simplification quota — hand a coding agent a hard, checkable target (LOC −30%) instead of a vague 'clean this up'
grabs.why: You run local AI agents for coding on your own stack; a deletion quota flips the agent from code generator to pruner, and a numeric target is trivially verifiable in a pipeline (wc -l before/after) before anything touches main. Cheap to port, no new dependency.

grabs.what: PR-shaped agent deliverable — spec the agent's output as a pull request or PR series rather than chat prose
grabs.why: Directly implements your 'structured in/out — prose is for humans, data is for machines' rule: the agent emits reviewable diffs your existing git workflow already consumes. Works with self-hosted git and offline models alike; nothing to buy, just a convention to adopt in your agent prompts.

aspects: Quantified deletion quota: define agent work as a measurable reduction target (e.g., −30% LOC) so success is mechanically checkable and the model biases toward removal over addition
Reviewable-artifact delivery: constrain agent output to the artifact your review pipeline already consumes (PR/PR series/diff) instead of freeform prose
Outcome-over-shape spec: state the required end state and let the executor choose decomposition granularity (monolithic vs. staged batches)
adjacency_queries: Prompt templates that give coding agents a measurable success metric like line, token, or dependency reduction instead of vague cleanup goals
Self-hosted tools that turn LLM output directly into git commits, patches, or PRs rather than chat responses
Document-processing pipeline patterns where an agent must compress input to a hard output budget (e.g., markdown to fixed-size structured summaries)
Task spec formats that define only the outcome and leave batch decomposition strategy to the executing agent

finds.name: prompt-compress — autoresearch compression loop (CLAUDE.md)
finds.what_it_is: A CLAUDE.md spec that drives an autonomous loop rewriting production system prompts to the shortest version that still passes a scoring gate: >=0.92 average semantic similarity vs baseline outputs, >=0.85 per-input floor. Token count is the minimized objective; a scoring script is the referee.
finds.different_angle: Same mechanism as the triaged directive — a hard numeric reduction target paired with an acceptance constraint — but transplanted from code to prompts, and with an open-ended minimize quota instead of a fixed 30%, gated by behavior preservation rather than review.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: You run local agents driven by plain-text specs; this is a copy-pasteable markdown file (no product, no account) demonstrating how to port the deletion-quota pattern to any domain that has a scoring script — directly applicable to your agent configs and ingest pipeline.

finds.name: reducing-entropy agent skill
finds.what_it_is: MIT-licensed installable skill (npx skills add softaworks/agent-toolkit) for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot and Antigravity that acts as an architectural gatekeeper: every change is evaluated by comparing total line count, prioritizing codebase minimization over incremental growth.
finds.different_angle: Turns the triaged item's one-shot deletion quota into a persistent rule enforced on every diff — the metric lives in the agent's standing instructions as a skill rather than in a per-task prompt.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: You run coding agents against your own repos and value small composable tools; a cross-tool skill file is plain-text, portable between your agents, and installs the LOC-quota mechanism with no new service or account.

finds.name: METR Task Standard
finds.what_it_is: An open (MIT, 187-star) standard from METR for defining agent tasks: each task is a self-contained environment with an outcome specification and programmatic scoring, so success is machine-checkable independently of how the agent gets there.
finds.different_angle: Same outcome-only-spec mechanism as the triaged directive — define the result, leave decomposition strategy to the executor — but formalized as a reproducible standard with verifiable scoring instead of a prose imperative and a eyeball-checked PR.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: Gives you a rigorous, git-versionable template for wrapping your own agent jobs (refactors, document processing) in acceptance criteria the machine can check — spec-as-data rather than spec-as-prose.

finds.name: autogit
finds.what_it_is: MIT-licensed CLI (62 stars) that hooks the end of an AI coding agent's turn and automatically stages, commits, and pushes, with a user-selected safety level.
finds.different_angle: Attacks the other half of the triaged mechanism — the structured deliverable. Instead of instructing the agent to produce PRs, it moves the routing into infrastructure: agent output lands in the normal git workflow by default, with the safety setting standing in for review control.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: You live in the terminal and run agents on local repos; this is a small single-purpose tool that composes with any agent and keeps your history in plain git instead of a vendor's session cloud.

finds.name: mdcompress
finds.what_it_is: A small Go library + CLI (MIT) that strips fluff from markdown files and emits a token-optimized version, built to cut LLM input costs on docs-heavy contexts.
finds.different_angle: The deletion quota implemented deterministically — no model call, no prompt: pure code enforces the reduction on markdown input, the way the triaged spec enforces it on code via an agent. The quota as a pipeline stage rather than a task instruction.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: Your ingest pipeline is markdown-in/structured-out and you prefer cheap single-purpose composable tools; this slots directly in front of your local models as a pre-compression stage with no API dependency.
